paragraphs.text: A loose leaf [Phoenix Dancong](dancong:definition), the [oolong](oolong:definition) of Fenghuang Shan in Chaozhou, eastern Guangdong. The name means [single bush](dancong:name): the leaf of one bush picked and made on its own, from the old Shuixian plants of the mountain. Dancong is withered in the sun, then [shaken and rested in rounds](dancong:making) to bruise the leaf edge, fixed at high heat, rolled into long strips and roasted, traditionally over charcoal.
Fresh Dancong is usually [rested for some months](dancong:ageing) after its roast before it is drunk. This leaf has been kept for more than fifty years.

brewing.text: Brew it gongfu style in a small gaiwan or clay pot, with about 3 to 8 grams for 100 to 120 ml and hot water, about 88 to 100°C; Chinese accounts mostly say 95 to 100°C. A quick rinse is common. Steeps start at a few seconds and grow a few seconds each round, and a good Dancong gives about eight to fifteen. Too long, too hot or too much leaf and it turns bitter and astringent.

notice.text: A smooth, mellow and sweet cup, often with dried fruit or plum and wood, sometimes something herbal, little astringency, and an amber to red-brown liquor.
